newsitem.title: USA: Merrill probe of ex-consultant inadequate - CFTC.
newsitem.headline: Merrill probe of ex-consultant inadequate - CFTC.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc.'s securities business unit conducted an inadequate investigation of the outside activities of a former employee who admitted defrauding some 110 investors out of about $8 million, a federal regulatory agency reported Wednesday.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commmission said the Merrill Lynch Pierce, Fenner & Smith Co. Inc. unit did not fulfil its supervisory obligations under federal regulations regarding former employee Richard Conroy Bell.

From 1990 to November 1993, while employed as a Merrill Lynch financial consultant, Bell operated a Ponzi scheme, defrauding about 110 investors in a commodity pool of about $8 million, the commission said.

A spokeswoman for Merrill in New York said, "To suggest that we were somehow remiss in not investigating these outside activities stretches the bounds of imagination as far as supervision is concerned."
A Ponzi scheme is a fraudulent pyramid-type scheme that involves luring investors seeking high returns to invest and using their funds to pay off earlier investors.
Bell pleaded guilty in 1994 to a federal wire-fraud charge and is serving a 44-month prison term, the commission said.
Instead of taking enforcement action against Merrill, the commission decided to make its 13-page investigative report public, Aronow said.
"Merrill Lynch did not consent to this report and disagrees with its conclusions," the spokeswoman said, adding Bell was convicted for activities that did not involve Merill Lynch or its clients.
